quotes.quote: Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 5 9(e), Plaintiff Qorvo, Inc. (“Qorvo”) respectfully moves t his Court to amend and/or alter the Judgment as entered against defendants Akoustis Technologies, Inc. and Akoustis, Inc. (collectively, “Akoustis”) on May 20, 2024 (D.I. 602)
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion to alter or amend the 20 May 2024 judgment (D.I. 611)

quotes.quote: The jury’s verdict should be amended to reflect “Yes” under Question 2(a), finding that Akoustis violated the UDTPA in connection with misappropriation of Qorvo’s trade secret and confidential information
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion to alter or amend the 20 May 2024 judgment (D.I. 611)

quotes.quote: By automatic trebling, the Court should amend the Judgment to award Qorvo $93,945,645 in compensatory damages in connection with its trade secret and UDTPA claims in aggregate.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion to alter or amend the 20 May 2024 judgment (D.I. 611)

quotes.quote: the jury awarded Qorvo $31,315,215 in “actual damages” under the NCTSPA based on Akoustis’s unjust enrichment, and the UDTPA automatically trebles any “damages” awarded by the jury.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion to alter or amend the 20 May 2024 judgment (D.I. 611)

quotes.quote: hereby moves the Court to award Qorvo its reasonable attorneys’ fees in accordance with the Defendant Trade Secrets Act (18 U.S.C. § 1836) and the North Carolina Trade Secret Protection Act (N.C.G.S. § 66-154(d)). In total, Qorvo seeks to recover $12,116,123.30 in reasonable attorneys’ fees.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion for attorneys' fees (D.I. 618)

quotes.quote: Qorvo further moves for its reasonable attorneys’ fees, to the extent not otherwise recoverable under the trade secrets statutes, pursuant to the North Carolina Unfair and Deceptive Trade Practices Act (N.C.G.S. § 75-16.1) contingent upon the Court granting judgment as a matter of law in Qorvo’s favor on its unfair trade practices claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion for attorneys' fees (D.I. 618)

quotes.quote: Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 59, defendants Akoustis Technologies, Inc. and Akoustis Inc. ( collectively “Akoustis” or the “Akoustis Defendants”) respectfully move the Court for an Order granting a new trial (or alternatively remittitur)
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis motion for a new trial or remittitur (D.I. 613)

quotes.quote: Ms. Bennis’ unreliable testimony requires that this Court order a new trial on damages, or alternatively
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis motion for a new trial or remittitur (D.I. 613)

quotes.quote: remittitur based on the unjust enrichment calculation submitted by Akoustis’ damages expert in the amount of $305,000.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis motion for a new trial or remittitur (D.I. 613)

quotes.quote: 2. Counts I and II, alleging patent infringement. The jury’s verdict was against the clear weight of the evidence presented at trial and constitutes a manifest miscarriage of justice.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis motion for a new trial or remittitur (D.I. 613)

quotes.quote: WHEREAS, Plaintiff currently intends to file a motion for entry of a permanent injunction and/or an ongoing royalty, and any other equitable relief that may be just and proper; a motion for pre-judgment and post -judgment interest; a motion for enhanced damages; a motion for attorneys’ fees and costs; and a motion to amend or alter the judgment with respect to the unfair competition claim;
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Stipulated order on the post-trial briefing schedule (D.I. 605)

quotes.quote: WHEREAS, Defendants currently intend to file motions under Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(b) and 59;
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Stipulated order on the post-trial briefing schedule (D.I. 605)

quotes.quote: Opening Briefs: On or before Monday, June 17, 2024 Answering Briefs: On or before Thursday, July 25, 2024 Reply Briefs: On or before Thursday, August 8, 2024
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Stipulated order on the post-trial briefing schedule (D.I. 605)

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. nodes.question: Does the court enter the requested trade-secret injunction?
nodes.label: Injunction

steps.text: eBay Inc. v. MercExchange, L.L.C., 547 U.S. 388 (2006): a permanent injunction issues where the plaintiff shows irreparable injury, inadequate remedies at law, a balance of hardships in its favour, and that the public interest would not be disserved.

18 U.S.C. §1836(b)(3)(A) (DTSA): in a civil action for trade-secret misappropriation a court "may" grant an injunction to prevent any actual or threatened misappropriation, on such terms as the court deems reasonable.

N.C. Gen. Stat. §66-154(a): actual or threatened misappropriation of a trade secret "shall be permanently enjoined upon judgment finding misappropriation" for the period the trade secret exists plus any further period the court deems necessary.
Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(c)(1): unless the court orders otherwise, an interlocutory or final judgment in an action for an injunction is not stayed after being entered, even if an appeal is taken.

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a)(1): a money judgment is enforced by a writ of execution; the procedure must accord with the procedure of the state where the court is located.

28 U.S.C. §1963: a judgment may be registered in another district "when the judgment has become final by appeal or expiration of the time for appeal or when ordered by the court that entered the judgment for good cause shown." steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a)(1): a money judgment is enforced by a writ of execution; the procedure must accord with the procedure of the state where the court is located.

28 U.S.C. §1963: a judgment may be registered in another district "when the judgment has become final by appeal or expiration of the time for appeal or when ordered by the court that entered the judgment for good cause shown." Good cause: thin forum assets and substantial assets elsewhere (Associated Bus. Tel. Sys. v. Greater Capital Corp., 128 F.R.D. 63, 66-68 (D.N.J. 1989)).

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a)(1): a money judgment is enforced by a writ of execution; the procedure must accord with the procedure of the state where the court is located.

the debtor's stated options: equity, debt, asset financing, collaborations or licensing, a sale or strategic transaction, restructuring or insolvency

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

nodes.question: Does the court approve the offered security and stay execution?

nodes.label: Stay approved

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

quotes.quote: Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 5 9(e), Plaintiff Qorvo, Inc. (“Qorvo”) respectfully moves t his Court to amend and/or alter the Judgment as entered against defendants Akoustis Technologies, Inc. and Akoustis, Inc. (collectively, “Akoustis”) on May 20, 2024 (D.I. 602)
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion to alter or amend the 20 May 2024 judgment (D.I. 611)

quotes.quote: The jury’s verdict should be amended to reflect “Yes” under Question 2(a), finding that Akoustis violated the UDTPA in connection with misappropriation of Qorvo’s trade secret and confidential information
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion to alter or amend the 20 May 2024 judgment (D.I. 611)

quotes.quote: By automatic trebling, the Court should amend the Judgment to award Qorvo $93,945,645 in compensatory damages in connection with its trade secret and UDTPA claims in aggregate.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion to alter or amend the 20 May 2024 judgment (D.I. 611)

quotes.quote: the jury awarded Qorvo $31,315,215 in “actual damages” under the NCTSPA based on Akoustis’s unjust enrichment, and the UDTPA automatically trebles any “damages” awarded by the jury.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion to alter or amend the 20 May 2024 judgment (D.I. 611)

quotes.quote: hereby moves the Court to award Qorvo its reasonable attorneys’ fees in accordance with the Defendant Trade Secrets Act (18 U.S.C. § 1836) and the North Carolina Trade Secret Protection Act (N.C.G.S. § 66-154(d)). In total, Qorvo seeks to recover $12,116,123.30 in reasonable attorneys’ fees.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion for attorneys' fees (D.I. 618)

quotes.quote: Qorvo further moves for its reasonable attorneys’ fees, to the extent not otherwise recoverable under the trade secrets statutes, pursuant to the North Carolina Unfair and Deceptive Trade Practices Act (N.C.G.S. § 75-16.1) contingent upon the Court granting judgment as a matter of law in Qorvo’s favor on its unfair trade practices claims.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Qorvo motion for attorneys' fees (D.I. 618)

quotes.quote: Pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 59, defendants Akoustis Technologies, Inc. and Akoustis Inc. ( collectively “Akoustis” or the “Akoustis Defendants”) respectfully move the Court for an Order granting a new trial (or alternatively remittitur)
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis motion for a new trial or remittitur (D.I. 613)

quotes.quote: Ms. Bennis’ unreliable testimony requires that this Court order a new trial on damages, or alternatively
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis motion for a new trial or remittitur (D.I. 613)

quotes.quote: remittitur based on the unjust enrichment calculation submitted by Akoustis’ damages expert in the amount of $305,000.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis motion for a new trial or remittitur (D.I. 613)

quotes.quote: 2. Counts I and II, alleging patent infringement. The jury’s verdict was against the clear weight of the evidence presented at trial and constitutes a manifest miscarriage of justice.
